text:
marta: Quick question — for the new routing policy canary, are we leaning REST+JSON at the gateway or gRPC+proto end-to-end?
kevin: my vote is gRPC for internal; simpler to version enums and avoids brittle JSON mapping.
samir: agreed on versioning but curious about quota propagation. With gRPC we still need a gateway to add rate-limiter headers for external teams, right?
julia: we could keep a tiny edge proxy that translates external REST -> internal gRPC, it only adds auth/quota headers. Sidecar everywhere feels heavy.
ben: +1 to the translator edge. Less churn for client teams. But we need to be explicit about which headers we canonicalize.
marta: important: telemetry. Console needs route-level latency broken down by transport hop and by policy. If we hide translation, will it confuse metrics?
kevin: we can emit x-rtg-policy and x-transport tags on spans. Example header rewrite we use in envoy:```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        request_handle:headers():add('x-rtg-policy', 'canary-v1')
      end
```
samir: Nice. For quota we add x-tenant-id and x-rate-key before calling internal token bucket service. That keeps quota semantics consistent regardless of transport.
julia: Rollout UX: we should surface canary percentage + transport fallback in the console. Teams will want one-click rollback to rest-only if something weird shows up.
ben: Agreed. Also add an auto-fallback rule: if gRPC latency p50 > 200ms for 30s, shift 10% to REST bridge for affected tenant. We can implement as a routing policy in the control plane.
marta: That implies the control plane needs real-time telemetry and an actuator for rollout weights. Do we have safe APIs for weight changes?
kevin: control-plane API exists: POST /v1/routes/{id}/weights with body {"variant":"canary-v1","weight":10}. It's currently HTTP JSON. We could keep it and have the router consume it, irrespective of internal transport.
samir: Edge-case: protobuf schema evolution — if we add a required enum, old sidecars will break. We must adopt non-breaking guidelines and stable backward-compatible enums. Also publish a deterministic compatibility lint in CI.
julia: Could we use proto wrappers that include a version header so gateways can detect incompatibility and fail open to REST bridge? e.g., x-proto-version: 2
ben: +1. Also add a monitoring alert when 'failed-deserialize' spikes. That will be our signal for schema regression.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: canary-v1 -> 5% traffic at 6120001240 :rocket:
infra-bot: Metrics stream enabled for route /api/routeX (tags: x-rtg-policy, x-transport, tenant)
marta: Perfect. After we collect 10m of telemetry, let's reconvene and decide gRPC-first vs keep dual-support. For now plan: gRPC internal, small REST translator at edge, real-time weight actuator + console controls.
kevin: I'll open a short RFC with the header list, control-plane API shape, and canary actuator details.
samir: I'll add the proto-lint CI job and compatibility checklist.
julia: I'll sketch the console wireframe for the canary card (percentage slider, fallback rules, recent anomalies).
ben: Thanks all. Ping me if you want the rollback playbook written into runbooks.
marta: awesome — tagging follow-ups: @kevin @samir @julia.
kevin: noted, will share RFC by EOD. :thumbsup:
